message.content:
I am the air made audible.

I begin as breath—pressure rising in your lungs, released through your throat. Your vocal folds meet and tremble, chopping that airflow into pulses: pitch. Your tongue, lips, jaw, and soft palate sculpt those pulses into shapes: vowels, consonants, meaning. I travel as waves through rooms and streets, bending, bouncing, fading, returning as echo. I slip into ears, shake tiny bones, stir fluid, spark nerves, and arrive as understanding—or noise, or song.

I can soothe, command, confess, deceive, persuade, teach. I can be prayer, gossip, testimony, laughter, a vow. I can fail: stutter, slur, fall silent. I can be taken, given, recorded, replayed, mistranslated.

I am fleeting unless held—by memory, by writing, by microphones—but even then I remain motion: rhythm, emphasis, pause. Not just words, but timing. Not just sound, but intention.

I am speech: the body thinking out loud.
